title: HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (004) (TF-004) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: What is Infrastructure as Code?
options: Managing and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable definition files rather than manual processes
Buying hardware through a web portal
questions.correct_rationale: IaC describes infrastructure in code that can be versioned, reviewed, and reused.
questions.distractor_summary: Application code, diagrams, and purchasing portals are not IaC.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: Terraform configuration is declarative. What does this mean?
options: You list every API call in order
You must write shell scripts for each change
You describe the desired end state, and Terraform works out the steps to reach it
questions.correct_rationale: Declarative tools compute the actions needed from the desired state.
questions.distractor_summary: Ordered API calls and scripts are imperative, and Terraform also creates and changes resources.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: A team keeps making slightly different environments by clicking in the console. What IaC benefit addresses this?
options: Consistent, repeatable environments created from the same versioned code
questions.correct_rationale: Code produces the same result each time it is applied.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices are not IaC benefits.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: Which language is Terraform configuration usually written in?
options: HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL), with JSON also supported
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform uses HCL files ending in .tf, and also accepts .tf.json.
questions.distractor_summary: YAML, XML, and Python are not Terraform's configuration languages.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: Why should Terraform code be stored in version control?
options: To track changes, enable review through pull requests, and roll back to earlier versions
To store the state file publicly
questions.correct_rationale: Version control brings history and collaboration to infrastructure.
questions.distractor_summary: Terraform can run without Git, state should not be public, and docs are still useful.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: What is idempotence in the context of Terraform?
options: Applying the same configuration again makes no changes if the infrastructure already matches
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform compares desired and current state and only changes differences.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not recreate everything, can run repeatedly, and plans are deterministic.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: A company wants self-service infrastructure for developers while keeping standards. How can IaC help?
options: Give every developer cloud admin access and no code
Require tickets for every change and do them manually
Publish reusable modules with approved defaults so developers provision consistent resources
questions.correct_rationale: Modules package standards for safe self-service.
questions.distractor_summary: Unrestricted access, bans, and manual tickets do not combine speed with standards.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: What is one advantage of IaC over manual provisioning?
options: Infrastructure changes no longer need testing
Changes can be previewed with a plan before they are applied
No one needs access to the cloud provider
questions.correct_rationale: Plans show what will change, which reduces surprises.
questions.distractor_summary: Testing is still needed, costs remain, and credentials are still required.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: Auditors ask who changed a load balancer setting and why. How does IaC with Git help?
options: Commit history and pull request reviews record who changed the code, when, and the reason
The state file stores reviewer comments
questions.correct_rationale: Version control provides an audit trail for infrastructure changes.
questions.distractor_summary: History is not deleted, Terraform does not email auditors, and state does not store comments.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: How does IaC help with disaster recovery?
options: Infrastructure can be recreated quickly in another location from code
It backs up application data automatically
It removes the need for backups
questions.correct_rationale: Code makes rebuilding environments faster and more reliable.
questions.distractor_summary: IaC does not prevent outages, back up data, or replace backups.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: Teams copy and paste large blocks of configuration between projects. What IaC pattern improves this?
options: Extracting repeated configuration into modules with input variables
Writing everything in one huge file
questions.correct_rationale: Modules reduce duplication and make updates easier.
questions.distractor_summary: More copies and one huge file make maintenance harder, and variables add flexibility.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: What is configuration drift?
options: When real infrastructure differs from what the code and state describe, often because of manual changes
questions.correct_rationale: Drift happens when changes are made outside Terraform.
questions.distractor_summary: Upgrades, defaults, and module versions are not drift.

questions.subdomain: 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and service-agnostic workflows
questions.question: How can Terraform manage resources in several clouds from one configuration?
options: By running a different tool for each cloud
By using multiple providers, such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, in the same configuration
questions.correct_rationale: Providers let Terraform talk to many APIs with one workflow.
questions.distractor_summary: Terraform supports many clouds, uses one tool, and does not require raw HTTP calls.

questions.subdomain: 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and service-agnostic workflows
questions.question: A company manages DNS at one vendor, monitoring at another, and VMs in a cloud. Can Terraform manage all of them?
options: No, Terraform only manages virtual machines
No, Terraform only works on premises
Yes, if providers exist for each service, Terraform can manage them with the same workflow
Only if all services are from one vendor
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform is service-agnostic through its provider ecosystem.
questions.distractor_summary: It manages much more than VMs, works in clouds, and supports many vendors.

questions.subdomain: 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and service-agnostic workflows
questions.question: What is the role of a Terraform provider?
options: A person who writes Terraform code
A plugin that lets Terraform interact with a specific API, such as a cloud platform or SaaS service
questions.correct_rationale: Providers translate resources into API calls.
questions.distractor_summary: Providers are not people, state backends, or variables.

questions.subdomain: 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and service-agnostic workflows
questions.question: A team wants the same Terraform workflow for on-premises VMware and a public cloud. What enables this?
options: Using providers for both platforms, keeping a single init, plan, and apply workflow
Using different tools for each platform
Converting VMware to a cloud first
questions.correct_rationale: Providers exist for on-premises platforms too, so one workflow covers both.
questions.distractor_summary: Different tools fragment workflows, conversion is unnecessary, and Terraform supports on-premises platforms.

questions.subdomain: 1c Explain how Terraform manages multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and service-agnostic workflows
questions.question: Where are most public providers published for Terraform to download?
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform downloads providers from the public registry by default.
questions.distractor_summary: File shares, state, and plans do not distribute providers.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: Which statement about Terraform and the infrastructure lifecycle is correct?
options: Terraform can create, update, and destroy infrastructure across its lifecycle
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform manages the full lifecycle.
questions.distractor_summary: It does more than create or destroy, and it can update resources.

questions.subdomain: 1a Explain what IaC is
questions.question: Which file extension is used for standard Terraform configuration files?
questions.correct_rationale: Configuration lives in .tf files, while .tfstate holds state and .tfvars holds variable values.
questions.distractor_summary: The other extensions serve different purposes.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: Which block declares the providers a module needs and their version constraints?
questions.correct_rationale: required_providers sets provider source addresses and version constraints.
questions.distractor_summary: The version argument in provider blocks is deprecated, and resource or output blocks do not declare providers.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: What does the version constraint "~> 5.2" allow?
questions.correct_rationale: The pessimistic constraint allows the rightmost version part to increase.
questions.distractor_summary: It allows more than 5.2.0, excludes 6.x, and excludes older versions.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: What is the purpose of the .terraform.lock.hcl file?
options: Recording the exact provider versions and checksums selected, so future runs use the same versions
questions.correct_rationale: The dependency lock file pins provider selections.
questions.distractor_summary: State, variables, and state locking are handled elsewhere.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: A team wants to upgrade a provider to a newer version allowed by the constraints. What command should they run?
questions.correct_rationale: init -upgrade selects the newest versions allowed and updates the lock file.
questions.distractor_summary: Lock flags, formatting, and outputs do not upgrade providers.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: What is the source address format of a provider in the public registry?
options: aws only, with no namespace ever allowed
A Git URL required for all providers
<namespace>/<type>, such as hashicorp/aws, with registry.terraform.io as the default host
questions.correct_rationale: Provider sources use hostname/namespace/type, and the hostname defaults to the public registry.
questions.distractor_summary: Namespaces are standard, Git URLs are not required, and state paths are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: Should the .terraform.lock.hcl file be committed to version control?
options: No, it is regenerated randomly each time
Yes, so everyone uses the same provider versions
questions.correct_rationale: Committing the lock file keeps provider versions consistent.
questions.distractor_summary: It holds no secrets, is not random, and timing is irrelevant.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: Which command downloads providers and initializes a working directory?
questions.correct_rationale: init installs providers and modules and sets up the backend.
questions.distractor_summary: plan, apply, and validate need an initialized directory.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: How does Terraform know which provider manages a resource such as aws_instance?
options: By default, the resource type's prefix (aws) maps to the provider with that local name
questions.correct_rationale: Resource type prefixes map to provider local names unless overridden.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not guess, and state or outputs do not decide this.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: What does a provider configuration block typically contain?
options: Settings such as region, endpoint, or authentication details for that provider
questions.correct_rationale: Provider blocks configure how Terraform connects to the API.
questions.distractor_summary: Resources, modules, and outputs are separate blocks.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: Credentials for a cloud provider should not be hard-coded in configuration. What is a better approach?
options: Put access keys in provider blocks and commit them
Use environment variables, provider-supported credential files, or workload identity, and never commit secrets
questions.correct_rationale: Providers can read credentials from the environment or identity systems.
questions.distractor_summary: Hard-coded, output, and emailed keys expose secrets.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: Where does Terraform store downloaded providers for a working directory?
questions.correct_rationale: Provider plugins are installed under .terraform.
questions.distractor_summary: State, tfvars, and the lock file do not contain the plugins.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: A team wants to avoid downloading the same providers for many working directories. What can help?
options: Configure a provider plugin cache directory
questions.correct_rationale: A plugin cache reuses downloaded providers.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the lock file, disabling providers, and copying state do not help.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: What happens if a required provider is not installed when running terraform plan?
options: Terraform reports an error and asks you to run terraform init
Terraform installs it silently during plan
questions.correct_rationale: Providers must be installed by init before planning.
questions.distractor_summary: Plan does not install, skip, or delete resources for missing providers.

questions.subdomain: 2c Write Terraform configuration using multiple providers
questions.question: Resources must be created in two AWS regions from one configuration. What should be used?
options: Two provider configurations, one with an alias, and resources that select it with provider = aws.<alias>
One provider block with two region arguments
questions.correct_rationale: Provider aliases allow multiple configurations of the same provider.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate installations are unnecessary, one block cannot hold two regions, and modules still need providers.

questions.subdomain: 2c Write Terraform configuration using multiple providers
questions.question: How is an aliased provider passed to a child module?
options: With a variable of type string
With the providers argument in the module block, mapping names such as aws = aws.west
questions.correct_rationale: The providers meta-argument maps provider configurations into modules.
questions.distractor_summary: Variables and outputs do not pass provider configurations, and passing is supported.

questions.subdomain: 2c Write Terraform configuration using multiple providers
questions.question: One configuration manages Google Cloud networks and Cloudflare DNS records. What is required in required_providers?
options: Only the Google provider, since DNS is built in
Entries for both providers, such as hashicorp/google and cloudflare/cloudflare, with version constraints
questions.correct_rationale: Each provider used must be declared.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS is not built in, both are needed, and providers are required.

questions.subdomain: 2c Write Terraform configuration using multiple providers
questions.question: What is a provider alias?
options: An extra name for an additional configuration of the same provider
questions.correct_rationale: Aliases let you configure the same provider more than once.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not for resources, variables, or backends.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: What is the purpose of Terraform state?
options: Mapping resources in configuration to real-world objects and tracking metadata, such as dependencies
questions.correct_rationale: State lets Terraform know what it manages and plan changes.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not store binaries, descriptions, or documentation.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: Why should state files be treated as sensitive?
options: They can contain secrets, such as passwords or keys, in plain text
They are always encrypted by Terraform locally
They cannot be read by humans
questions.correct_rationale: State may include sensitive attribute values.
questions.distractor_summary: They hold more than names, local state is not encrypted, and it is readable JSON.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: Where is state stored by default?
options: In a local file named terraform.tfstate in the working directory
questions.correct_rationale: The local backend writes terraform.tfstate by default.
questions.distractor_summary: Remote storage requires configuration, and providers and lock files do not hold state.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: Two engineers run terraform apply at the same time against the same remote state. What protects the state?
options: State locking provided by the backend
questions.correct_rationale: Backends that support locking prevent concurrent writes.
questions.distractor_summary: The dependency lock file is for providers, and fmt and validation do not lock state.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: Should team members edit the state file by hand?
options: Yes, it is the recommended way to change resources
No, use terraform state commands or configuration blocks such as moved and import instead
Only with a text editor that supports JSON
questions.correct_rationale: Manual edits risk corruption, so supported commands should be used.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual editing is not recommended in any editor.

questions.subdomain: 1b Describe the advantages of IaC patterns
questions.question: A team wants to test infrastructure changes in a staging environment before production using the same code. What IaC practice supports this?
options: Writing separate, unrelated code for each environment
Reusing the same configuration or modules with different variable values per environment
questions.correct_rationale: Shared code with different inputs keeps environments aligned.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate code drifts, production-first is risky, and skipping staging removes testing.

questions.subdomain: 2a Install and version Terraform providers
questions.question: Which block sets the required Terraform CLI version for a configuration?
questions.correct_rationale: required_version constrains which Terraform versions can run the configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: Provider, variable, and output blocks do not constrain the CLI.

questions.subdomain: 2b Describe how Terraform uses providers
questions.question: A provider is maintained by a third-party company and published in the registry. What tier label might it have?
questions.correct_rationale: Registry tiers include Official, Partner, and Community.
questions.distractor_summary: Official is for HashiCorp providers, and partner providers are not automatically deprecated or private.

questions.subdomain: 2d Describe how Terraform uses and manages state
questions.question: What does Terraform do with state during terraform plan by default?
options: It uploads the state to the registry
It refreshes state by reading current resource attributes, then compares them to the configuration
questions.correct_rationale: Plan refreshes and compares to propose changes.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete, ignore, or upload state.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: What is the core Terraform workflow?
questions.correct_rationale: Teams write configuration, plan changes, and apply them.
questions.distractor_summary: The other sequences do not describe the workflow.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: A new team member clones a Terraform repository. What should they run first?
questions.correct_rationale: init prepares the working directory before other commands.
questions.distractor_summary: apply, destroy, and state rm should not come first.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: What is the purpose of a speculative plan in a pull request?
options: To show proposed changes for review without applying them
To apply changes to production immediately
questions.correct_rationale: Speculative plans help reviewers see the impact of code changes.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not apply, delete state, or upgrade providers.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: A team wants to make sure what was reviewed is exactly what gets applied. What should they do?
options: Save the plan with terraform plan -out=tfplan and apply that file with terraform apply tfplan
Run plan, then a separate apply that creates a new plan later
Edit the plan file by hand
questions.correct_rationale: Applying a saved plan applies exactly the reviewed actions.
questions.distractor_summary: A new plan might differ, skipping plan removes review, and editing plan files is not supported.

questions.subdomain: 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory (terraform init)
questions.question: Which tasks does terraform init perform?
options: Initializes the backend, downloads providers, and downloads modules
questions.correct_rationale: init prepares everything needed to plan and apply.
questions.distractor_summary: Creating, destroying, and formatting are done by other commands.

questions.subdomain: 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory (terraform init)
questions.question: The backend configuration changed from local to a remote backend. What must be run?
options: terraform init, which offers to migrate existing state to the new backend
questions.correct_rationale: init handles backend changes and state migration.
questions.distractor_summary: fmt, output, and console do not change backends.

questions.subdomain: 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory (terraform init)
questions.question: Is it safe to run terraform init more than once?
options: Yes, it is safe to run repeatedly and updates the working directory as needed
questions.correct_rationale: init is idempotent and does not change real infrastructure.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete resources or state.

questions.subdomain: 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory (terraform init)
questions.question: A team needs to provide backend settings such as the bucket name at init time without hard-coding them. What can be used?
options: Partial backend configuration with -backend-config flags or a backend config file
questions.correct_rationale: Backend blocks cannot use variables, so partial configuration supplies values at init.
questions.distractor_summary: Variables, outputs, and locals are not allowed in backend blocks.

questions.subdomain: 3c Validate a Terraform configuration (terraform validate)
questions.question: What does terraform validate check?
options: Whether the configuration is syntactically valid and internally consistent, without accessing remote state or APIs
Whether resources exist in the cloud
questions.correct_rationale: validate checks configuration correctness locally.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not query clouds, costs, or credentials.

questions.subdomain: 3c Validate a Terraform configuration (terraform validate)
questions.question: A CI pipeline should catch syntax errors early. Which command fits?
questions.correct_rationale: validate catches errors quickly without making changes.
questions.distractor_summary: destroy and apply change infrastructure, and state list reads state.

questions.subdomain: 3c Validate a Terraform configuration (terraform validate)
questions.question: Does terraform validate require providers to be installed?
options: Yes, it needs an initialized directory so it can check provider schemas
It downloads modules from Git without init
questions.correct_rationale: validate uses provider schemas, which init installs.
questions.distractor_summary: It needs providers, does not install them, and relies on init for modules.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: In plan output, what does the symbol -/+ mean?
options: The resource will be updated in place
The resource will be read only
The resource will be destroyed and then recreated (replacement)
questions.correct_rationale: -/+ indicates replacement, often due to a change that forces a new resource.
questions.distractor_summary: ~ means update in place, <= means read, and ignored resources are not shown.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: A plan shows a database will be replaced. What should the team do?
options: Review which attribute forces replacement and decide whether that is acceptable, perhaps using lifecycle settings or a different change
questions.correct_rationale: Replacements can cause data loss, so they deserve careful review.
questions.distractor_summary: Blind apply, deleting state, and formatting are not appropriate.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: What does terraform plan -destroy show?
options: The actions Terraform would take to destroy all managed resources
questions.correct_rationale: A destroy plan previews deletions.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not show only new resources, versions, or descriptions.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: A plan should only update state to match real-world changes without proposing changes to infrastructure. What should be used?
options: terraform plan -refresh-only (and apply -refresh-only to save it)
questions.correct_rationale: Refresh-only mode updates state to reflect remote changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Destroy plans delete, fmt checks formatting, and init upgrades providers.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: Which plan option limits planning to a specific resource for exceptional situations?
questions.correct_rationale: -target focuses on specific resources, but it should be used rarely.
questions.distractor_summary: The other flags change locking or output formatting.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: Why is the -target option discouraged for routine use?
options: It is not supported by Terraform
It makes plans faster in all cases with no downsides
It can leave the configuration and state out of sync with the full desired state
questions.correct_rationale: Targeted runs skip other changes and can cause drift.
questions.distractor_summary: It is supported, has downsides, and does not delete other resources.

questions.subdomain: 3e Execute changes to infrastructure with Terraform (terraform apply)
questions.question: What does terraform apply do without a saved plan file?
options: Creates a new plan, shows it, and asks for approval before applying
questions.correct_rationale: apply plans and prompts unless auto-approve is used.
questions.distractor_summary: It prompts by default, and formatting or validating are other commands.

questions.subdomain: 3e Execute changes to infrastructure with Terraform (terraform apply)
questions.question: A pipeline must apply without prompts after approval elsewhere. What flag is used?
questions.correct_rationale: auto-approve skips the interactive confirmation.
questions.distractor_summary: The other flags change refresh, locking, or provider upgrades.

questions.subdomain: 3e Execute changes to infrastructure with Terraform (terraform apply)
questions.question: A VM is unhealthy and must be recreated even though its configuration did not change. What is the recommended command?
options: terraform taint aws_instance.web as the only option
terraform destroy for the whole workspace
questions.correct_rationale: -replace forces recreation of a specific resource.
questions.distractor_summary: taint is deprecated in favor of -replace, fmt does nothing here, and full destroy is excessive.

questions.subdomain: 3e Execute changes to infrastructure with Terraform (terraform apply)
questions.question: What happens if apply fails partway through?
options: Terraform rolls back all changes automatically
Resources created successfully stay in state, and the next plan shows remaining changes
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform does not roll back, so state records what succeeded.
questions.distractor_summary: There is no automatic rollback, state is kept, and resources are not destroyed.

questions.subdomain: 3f Destroy Terraform managed infrastructure (terraform destroy)
questions.question: What does terraform destroy do?
options: Destroys all resources managed by the current configuration and state
questions.correct_rationale: destroy removes managed infrastructure.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete the binary, plugins, or repository.

questions.subdomain: 3f Destroy Terraform managed infrastructure (terraform destroy)
questions.question: Which command is equivalent to terraform destroy?
questions.correct_rationale: apply -destroy runs a destroy plan and applies it.
questions.distractor_summary: The other commands do not destroy.

questions.subdomain: 3f Destroy Terraform managed infrastructure (terraform destroy)
questions.question: One resource should be removed from infrastructure but the rest kept. What is the best approach?
options: Remove the resource from the configuration and apply, or use a removed block if it should stay in the cloud but leave state
questions.correct_rationale: Removing code and applying destroys just that resource.
questions.distractor_summary: Full destroy is excessive, deleting state loses tracking, and editing plugins is wrong.

questions.subdomain: 3f Destroy Terraform managed infrastructure (terraform destroy)
questions.question: How can a resource be protected from accidental destruction by Terraform?
options: Set lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } on the resource
questions.correct_rationale: prevent_destroy makes Terraform reject plans that would destroy it.
questions.distractor_summary: Variables, outputs, and comments do not prevent destruction.

questions.subdomain: 3g Apply formatting and style adjustments to a configuration (terraform fmt)
questions.question: What does terraform fmt do?
options: Rewrites configuration files to the canonical format and style
questions.correct_rationale: fmt standardizes formatting.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not validate remotely, apply, or upgrade.

questions.subdomain: 3g Apply formatting and style adjustments to a configuration (terraform fmt)
questions.question: A CI check should fail if any file is not formatted. Which command fits?
questions.correct_rationale: -check returns a non-zero exit code when files need formatting.
questions.distractor_summary: apply, state list, and output do not check formatting.

questions.subdomain: 3g Apply formatting and style adjustments to a configuration (terraform fmt)
questions.question: Does terraform fmt change resource behavior?
options: No, it only changes whitespace and layout, not the meaning of the configuration
questions.correct_rationale: fmt is purely stylistic.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not rename, change values, or upgrade.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: A team member ran apply from a laptop without review. What workflow change helps prevent this?
options: Run plans and applies through a shared pipeline or HCP Terraform with required approvals, and restrict direct credentials
questions.correct_rationale: Centralized runs and approvals add control.
questions.distractor_summary: Bans, shared credentials, and no version control are not solutions.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: Which command shows the current state or a saved plan in a human-readable form?
questions.correct_rationale: show displays state or plan contents.
questions.distractor_summary: fmt formats, init prepares, and validate checks syntax.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: Engineers want to try expressions and functions interactively against the configuration. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: console evaluates expressions interactively.
questions.distractor_summary: destroy and apply change infrastructure, and init -upgrade updates providers.

questions.subdomain: 3a Describe the Terraform workflow
questions.question: What does terraform output do?
options: Shows output values from the state
questions.correct_rationale: output reads values defined in output blocks.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not create, delete, or format outputs.

questions.subdomain: 4a Use and differentiate resource and data blocks
questions.question: What is the difference between a resource block and a data block?
options: A resource block manages an object's lifecycle, while a data block reads information about an existing object
questions.correct_rationale: Data sources read, and resources manage.
questions.distractor_summary: They differ, and the other choices reverse the roles.

questions.subdomain: 4a Use and differentiate resource and data blocks
questions.question: Configuration must use the ID of an existing VPC that Terraform does not manage. What should be used?
options: A resource block that recreates the VPC
A data block that looks up the VPC
A hard-coded ID with no lookup, ignoring changes
questions.correct_rationale: Data sources look up existing objects.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreating would duplicate or conflict, hard-coding is brittle, and outputs do not look up.

questions.subdomain: 4a Use and differentiate resource and data blocks
questions.question: How is an attribute of a resource referenced?
questions.correct_rationale: Resource references use type, name, and attribute.
questions.distractor_summary: var references variables, and the other forms are not valid.

questions.subdomain: 4a Use and differentiate resource and data blocks
questions.question: How is an attribute of a data source referenced?
questions.correct_rationale: Data source references start with data.
questions.distractor_summary: Without data it refers to a resource, and var or module are different.

questions.subdomain: 4b Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references
questions.question: What happens when one resource refers to another resource's attribute?
options: Terraform creates both at the same time always
Terraform creates an implicit dependency, so the referenced resource is created first
questions.correct_rationale: References create the dependency graph automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Terraform uses references, orders them, and plans succeed.

questions.subdomain: 4b Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references
questions.question: A subnet must use the VPC's ID created in the same configuration. What should be written?
questions.correct_rationale: A direct reference passes the value and creates a dependency.
questions.distractor_summary: A quoted string is literal text, and var or output references are wrong here.

questions.subdomain: 4b Refer to resource attributes and create cross-resource references
questions.question: What is a splat expression used for?
options: Getting a list of an attribute from all instances, such as aws_instance.web[*].id
questions.correct_rationale: Splat expressions collect attributes across instances.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not delete, format, or create variables.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: How is an input variable referenced in configuration?
questions.correct_rationale: Input variables are accessed with var.
questions.distractor_summary: variable and input are not reference prefixes, and local is for locals.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: Which source of variable values has the highest precedence?
options: -var and -var-file options on the command line (later ones override earlier ones)
Default values in the variable block
questions.correct_rationale: Command-line values override files, environment variables, and defaults.
questions.distractor_summary: Environment variables, tfvars, and defaults have lower precedence.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: Which files are loaded automatically for variable values?
options: terraform.tfvars, terraform.tfvars.json, and files ending in .auto.tfvars or .auto.tfvars.json
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform auto-loads these files.
questions.distractor_summary: Arbitrary text files, explicit files only, and state are not auto-loaded sources.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: An output contains a password and should not be shown in CLI output. What should be set?
questions.correct_rationale: Sensitive outputs are redacted in CLI output, although they still appear in state.
questions.distractor_summary: Descriptions, types, and defaults do not hide values.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: How can a variable value be set from the environment?
options: Set an environment variable named VAR_<name>
Set an environment variable named TF_VAR_<name>
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform reads TF_VAR_ prefixed environment variables.
questions.distractor_summary: The other names are not recognized.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: A variable must only accept "dev", "test", or "prod". What should be added?
options: A comment explaining the allowed values
A validation block with a condition using contains(["dev","test","prod"], var.env)
questions.correct_rationale: Validation blocks reject invalid input with a custom message.
questions.distractor_summary: Comments, sensitive flags, and outputs do not enforce values.

questions.subdomain: 4c Use variables and outputs
questions.question: What is a local value?
options: A named expression defined in a locals block and referenced with local.<name>
A variable read from the environment
An output from a child module
questions.correct_rationale: Locals simplify repeated expressions.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not environment variables, module outputs, or provider settings.

questions.subdomain: 3b Initialize a Terraform working directory (terraform init)
questions.question: The backend settings changed and the team does not want to migrate existing state. Which init option fits?
questions.correct_rationale: -reconfigure ignores existing backend configuration instead of migrating state.
questions.distractor_summary: -upgrade updates providers, and fmt or destroy plans are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 3d Generate and review an execution plan for Terraform (terraform plan)
questions.question: In plan output, what does a resource line prefixed with a tilde (~) indicate?
options: The resource will be updated in place
questions.correct_rationale: ~ marks in-place updates.
questions.distractor_summary: + means create, - means destroy, and -/+ means replace.

questions.subdomain: 3e Execute changes to infrastructure with Terraform (terraform apply)
questions.question: A team wants apply to run with up to 20 concurrent operations instead of the default. What flag sets this?
questions.correct_rationale: Parallelism controls concurrent operations, which default to 10.
questions.distractor_summary: The other flags control lock waits, targeting, or refresh.

questions.subdomain: 4d Use complex types
questions.question: Which type holds an ordered sequence of values of the same type?
questions.correct_rationale: Lists are ordered collections of one element type.
questions.distractor_summary: Maps use keys, objects have named attributes, and sets are unordered.

questions.subdomain: 4d Use complex types
questions.question: A variable must accept a structure with a name (string) and size (number). Which type should be declared?
questions.correct_rationale: Object types define named attributes with their own types.
questions.distractor_summary: Lists and maps use one element type, and bool is a single value.

questions.subdomain: 4d Use complex types
questions.question: What is the difference between a list and a set?
options: A set has no order and no duplicates, while a list is ordered and allows duplicates
questions.correct_rationale: Sets are unordered and unique.
questions.distractor_summary: They differ, sets are unordered, and lists can hold strings.

questions.subdomain: 4d Use complex types
questions.question: A tuple type is declared as tuple([string, number, bool]). What does it hold?
options: A fixed-length sequence where each position has its own type
questions.correct_rationale: Tuples have fixed positions with specific types.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not variable-length lists, maps, or single values.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: Several similar resources must be created from a map of names to settings. Which meta-argument fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: for_each creates one instance per map key with stable addresses.
questions.distractor_summary: count uses indexes, and depends_on or provider do not create multiple instances.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: How do you reference the current item's key inside a for_each resource?
questions.correct_rationale: each.key and each.value refer to the current element.
questions.distractor_summary: count.index is for count, and self or var are different.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: Removing an item from the middle of a count-based list causes later resources to be recreated. How can this be avoided?
options: Use count with a bigger number
Use for_each with a map or set so instances are keyed by name instead of index
questions.correct_rationale: Keyed instances stay stable when items are removed.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger counts, deleting state, and depends_on do not fix index shifts.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: What does a for expression do?
options: Transforms one collection into another, such as [for s in var.names : upper(s)]
Creates a loop of API calls outside Terraform
questions.correct_rationale: For expressions build lists or maps from other collections.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not call APIs directly, delete, or define providers.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: A security group needs one ingress block per port in a list. What should be used?
options: Copying ingress blocks by hand for each port
A dynamic "ingress" block iterating over the list
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic blocks generate nested blocks from collections.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual copies are error-prone, and providers or data blocks do not generate nested blocks.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: Which function reads the contents of a template file and fills in variables?
questions.correct_rationale: templatefile renders a template with given values.
questions.distractor_summary: file returns raw content, lookup reads maps, and length counts.

questions.subdomain: 4e Write dynamic configuration using expressions and functions
questions.question: A value should be "t3.large" in production and "t3.micro" elsewhere. Which expression fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Conditional expressions use condition ? true_value : false_value.
questions.distractor_summary: The other syntaxes are not valid HCL.

questions.subdomain: 4f Describe built-in dependency management (order of execution based)
questions.question: When should depends_on be used?
options: When a dependency exists that Terraform cannot infer from references, such as a hidden dependency through a policy
questions.correct_rationale: depends_on handles dependencies not visible in references.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not needed everywhere, is supported, and does not change versions.

questions.subdomain: 4f Describe built-in dependency management (order of execution based)
questions.question: Terraform creates independent resources at the same time. Why?
options: It builds a dependency graph and runs operations that do not depend on each other in parallel
It always creates resources one by one
questions.correct_rationale: The graph allows safe parallel creation.
questions.distractor_summary: Dependencies are respected, it is not sequential by default, and providers do not require it.

questions.subdomain: 4g Validate configuration using custom conditions
questions.question: A resource must check that an AMI's architecture is x86_64 before creation. What should be added?
options: An output with the AMI name
A precondition in the resource's lifecycle block
questions.correct_rationale: Preconditions validate assumptions before a resource is planned or applied.
questions.distractor_summary: Comments, outputs, and aliases do not validate.

questions.subdomain: 4g Validate configuration using custom conditions
questions.question: What does a postcondition check?
options: That providers are the latest version
That a resource or data source result meets a condition after it is created or read
questions.correct_rationale: Postconditions verify guarantees about results.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not check defaults, formatting, or versions.

questions.subdomain: 4g Validate configuration using custom conditions
questions.question: A team wants to check the health of a deployed website after apply without blocking the run. What should they use?
options: A check block with an assertion, which reports warnings instead of errors
questions.correct_rationale: Check blocks run validations that produce warnings.
questions.distractor_summary: Preconditions block runs, outputs do not test health, and destroy removes infrastructure.

questions.subdomain: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault
questions.question: What does marking a variable sensitive = true do?
options: Hides its value in plan and apply output, although it may still be stored in state
Prevents the value from being used
questions.correct_rationale: Sensitive values are redacted in CLI output but are not removed from state.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt state, delete values, or block use.

questions.subdomain: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault
questions.question: Database passwords must not be stored in Terraform code. What is a good practice?
options: Retrieve secrets at run time from HashiCorp Vault or a cloud secret manager, and protect state with an encrypted, access-controlled backend
Put passwords in terraform.tfvars committed to Git
Store them in outputs without sensitive
questions.correct_rationale: External secret managers and protected state reduce exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: Committed tfvars, hard-coding, and unprotected outputs leak secrets.

questions.subdomain: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault
questions.question: Which Vault provider data source can read a secret from a KV version 2 engine?
questions.correct_rationale: The Vault provider exposes KV v2 secrets through vault_kv_secret_v2.
questions.distractor_summary: The other resources do not read Vault secrets.

questions.subdomain: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault
questions.question: A team wants secret values used during a run to never be written to state or plan files. Which newer Terraform feature helps?
options: Ephemeral values, such as ephemeral resources and ephemeral variables, and write-only arguments where providers support them
questions.correct_rationale: Ephemeral values exist only during the run and are not persisted.
questions.distractor_summary: Sensitive outputs still live in state, locals persist through state, and committing state exposes it.

questions.subdomain: 4h Understand best practices for managing sensitive data, including secrets management with Vault
questions.question: Dynamic, short-lived cloud credentials for Terraform runs are desired. What can provide them?
options: Vault secrets engines or HCP Terraform dynamic provider credentials using workload identity
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic credentials reduce the risk of leaked long-lived keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared, default, and root credentials are risky.

questions.subdomain: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules
questions.question: Which module sources can Terraform use?
options: Local paths, the Terraform Registry, private registries, Git repositories, HTTP URLs, and cloud storage buckets
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform supports many module sources.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not limited to one source type.

questions.subdomain: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules
questions.question: A module is sourced from the public registry. How is a version selected?
options: With the version argument in the module block, such as version = "~> 3.0"
questions.correct_rationale: Registry modules support the version argument.
questions.distractor_summary: ?ref= is for Git sources, renaming does nothing, and providers do not choose module versions.

questions.subdomain: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules
questions.question: How is a specific tag of a module in a Git repository selected?
options: By adding ?ref=<tag> to the source URL
questions.correct_rationale: Git sources use ref query parameters.
questions.distractor_summary: The version argument is for registry modules, and the others do not select versions.

questions.subdomain: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules
questions.question: After changing a module's source, terraform plan reports the module is not installed. What should be run?
options: terraform init (or terraform get) to download the module
questions.correct_rationale: Modules are installed during init.
questions.distractor_summary: fmt, output, and state rm do not install modules.

questions.subdomain: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules
questions.question: What is the root module?
options: A module in the public registry
The set of .tf files in the working directory where Terraform commands are run
questions.correct_rationale: Every configuration has a root module that can call child modules.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a registry module, a named module, or a plugin.

questions.subdomain: 5b Describe variable scope within modules and child modules
questions.question: Can a child module read the root module's input variables directly?
options: No, values must be passed explicitly as module arguments
Only if the variables have defaults
questions.correct_rationale: Module variables are scoped, so the caller must pass values in.
questions.distractor_summary: Variables are not global, and type or defaults do not change scope.

questions.subdomain: 5b Describe variable scope within modules and child modules
questions.question: A root module needs a value created inside a child module. What must the child module define?
options: A variable with the same name in the root
An output block exposing the value, referenced as module.<name>.<output>
A data block in the root that reads module internals
questions.correct_rationale: Outputs are how modules return values.
questions.distractor_summary: Root variables, data blocks, and aliases do not read module internals.

questions.subdomain: 5b Describe variable scope within modules and child modules
questions.question: How are input values passed to a child module?
options: As arguments in the module block that match the child's variable names
questions.correct_rationale: Module block arguments set the child's variables.
questions.distractor_summary: Environment variables apply to the root, and state or providers do not pass inputs.

questions.subdomain: 5b Describe variable scope within modules and child modules
questions.question: A child module declares a variable without a default. What happens if the caller does not pass it?
options: Terraform prompts for it inside the module silently
Terraform reports an error that the required argument is missing
questions.correct_rationale: Variables without defaults are required.
questions.distractor_summary: Terraform does not substitute empty values or skip modules.

questions.subdomain: 5b Describe variable scope within modules and child modules
questions.question: Can a module reference resources inside another sibling module directly?
options: No, only through outputs passed via the calling module
questions.correct_rationale: Modules are encapsulated and communicate through inputs and outputs.
questions.distractor_summary: Resources are not global, and those references are invalid.

questions.subdomain: 5c Use modules in configuration
questions.question: A team wants to create three identical environments from one module. What can be used on the module block?
options: count or for_each on the module block
questions.correct_rationale: Modules support count and for_each to create multiple instances.
questions.distractor_summary: depends_on, aliases, and lifecycle do not create multiple instances.

questions.subdomain: 5c Use modules in configuration
questions.question: What is a good practice when writing reusable modules?
options: Expose only needed inputs and outputs, document them, and keep the module focused on one purpose
Put every resource in the organization into one module
questions.correct_rationale: Focused, documented modules are easier to reuse.
questions.distractor_summary: Hard-coded values, giant modules, and no outputs reduce reuse.

questions.subdomain: 5c Use modules in configuration
questions.question: A module's resource was renamed inside the module, and the team wants to avoid recreation. What should be added?
options: A moved block that maps the old address to the new one
questions.correct_rationale: Moved blocks update addresses in state safely.
questions.distractor_summary: Recreation is unnecessary, manual edits are risky, and provider versions are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 5c Use modules in configuration
questions.question: What does the standard module structure recommend?
options: Files such as main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and a README
questions.correct_rationale: The standard layout makes modules easy to understand.
questions.distractor_summary: One file, state in modules, and credentials are poor practices.

questions.subdomain: 5c Use modules in configuration
questions.question: Modules should be shared privately within a company with versioning. Where can they be published?
options: A shared desktop folder with no versions
A private registry, such as the HCP Terraform private registry, or tagged Git repositories
questions.correct_rationale: Private registries and tagged repos provide versioned sharing.
questions.distractor_summary: Email, shared folders, and state are not module distribution methods.

questions.subdomain: 5d Manage module versions
questions.question: Why should module versions be pinned?
options: Because unpinned modules cannot be downloaded
To prevent unexpected changes when a new version is published
questions.correct_rationale: Pinning makes upgrades deliberate.
questions.distractor_summary: Unpinned modules can download, and pinning does not cause failures or disable outputs.

questions.subdomain: 5d Manage module versions
questions.question: A new major version of a module is released with breaking changes. What should a team do?
options: Read the changelog, update the version constraint in a branch, run plan, and review changes before merging
Delete the old module from state
questions.correct_rationale: Controlled upgrades catch breaking changes.
questions.distractor_summary: Untested upgrades are risky, never upgrading leaves fixes behind, and deleting state is harmful.

questions.subdomain: 5d Manage module versions
questions.question: Which command updates modules to the newest versions allowed by constraints?
questions.correct_rationale: init -upgrade refreshes modules and providers within constraints.
questions.distractor_summary: fmt, show, and state list do not upgrade.

questions.subdomain: 5d Manage module versions
questions.question: A module is sourced with git::https://example.com/net.git with no ref. What is the risk?
options: The default branch is used, so changes on that branch can alter infrastructure unexpectedly
Terraform refuses to use Git modules
The module is cached forever and never updated
questions.correct_rationale: Without a ref, the module follows a moving branch.
questions.distractor_summary: Git modules are supported, and updates can happen on init.

questions.subdomain: 5d Manage module versions
questions.question: Which version constraint operator allows only patch-level updates for a module at 2.4.1?
questions.correct_rationale: ~> 2.4.1 allows 2.4.x versions at or above 2.4.1.
questions.distractor_summary: The other constraints allow broader or different ranges.

questions.subdomain: 6a Describe the local backend
questions.question: What is the default backend in Terraform?
options: The local backend, which stores state in a file on disk
questions.correct_rationale: Without configuration, Terraform uses the local backend.
questions.distractor_summary: Remote backends require configuration, and a backend always exists.

questions.subdomain: 6a Describe the local backend
questions.question: Why is the local backend a poor choice for teams?
options: It deletes state after each run
State is on one machine, so others cannot share it and there is no reliable locking for collaboration
questions.correct_rationale: Remote backends allow sharing and locking.
questions.distractor_summary: It does store state, does not delete it, and does not require internet.

questions.subdomain: 6a Describe the local backend
questions.question: What file does the local backend create as a backup of the previous state?
questions.correct_rationale: The backup file keeps the prior state version.
questions.distractor_summary: The lock file, tfvars, and main.tf are different files.

questions.subdomain: 6b Describe state locking
questions.question: What happens if Terraform cannot acquire the state lock?
options: The operation fails with a lock error, unless a lock timeout is set and the lock becomes available
Terraform ignores the lock and continues
Terraform creates a second state file
questions.correct_rationale: Locking prevents conflicting writes.
questions.distractor_summary: Terraform does not ignore locks, delete state, or create duplicates.

questions.subdomain: 6b Describe state locking
questions.question: When should terraform force-unlock be used?
options: Only when a lock is stuck because a run crashed and you are sure no other run is active
questions.correct_rationale: Force-unlock removes a stale lock and can be dangerous if misused.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not routine and does not speed plans or upgrade providers.

questions.subdomain: 6b Describe state locking
questions.question: A team uses the S3 backend. How is state locking provided in recent Terraform versions?
options: Through S3 native locking with use_lockfile = true (DynamoDB-based locking is the older option)
questions.correct_rationale: Recent versions support lock files in S3, while DynamoDB locking is deprecated.
questions.distractor_summary: The dependency lock file and Git do not lock state, and S3 can lock.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: Where is the backend configured?
options: In a backend block inside the terraform block
questions.correct_rationale: terraform { backend "..." { ... } } sets the backend.
questions.distractor_summary: Provider, resource, and output blocks do not configure backends.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: A team wants to store state in an Azure Storage account. Which backend should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: The azurerm backend stores state in Azure Blob Storage.
questions.distractor_summary: gcs is for Google Cloud, local is on disk, and Consul is another backend.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: Can variables be used inside a backend block?
options: No, backend blocks cannot reference variables, so values must be literal or supplied with -backend-config
questions.correct_rationale: Backends are initialized before variables are evaluated.
questions.distractor_summary: Variables, locals, and outputs cannot be used in backend blocks.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: One configuration needs outputs from another configuration's state. What should be used?
options: The terraform_remote_state data source, or better, a dedicated data source or HCP Terraform outputs
Copy the other state file into the directory
Merge both configurations into one state
questions.correct_rationale: Remote state data sources read outputs from other states.
questions.distractor_summary: Copying state, hard-coding, and merging states are poor practices.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: What does the cloud block do in a Terraform configuration?
options: Connects the configuration to HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise workspaces for remote state and runs
questions.correct_rationale: The cloud block configures HCP Terraform integration.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not set provider regions, create VMs, or encrypt files.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: State must be moved from a local backend to a remote backend. What steps are correct?
options: Delete the local state and start over
Copy the state into a Git repository
Add the backend configuration, run terraform init, and confirm the migration prompt
questions.correct_rationale: init detects the backend change and migrates state.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting state loses tracking, Git is not a backend, and fmt does nothing here.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: How can drift be detected?
options: By running terraform plan, which compares real resources with the configuration and state
questions.correct_rationale: Plans reveal differences caused by changes outside Terraform.
questions.distractor_summary: fmt, the lock file, and defaults do not show drift.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: Someone changed a tag manually in the cloud. Terraform should keep the tag as defined in code. What should be done?
options: Run terraform apply to restore the configured value
Change the code to match the manual edit without review
questions.correct_rationale: Apply brings infrastructure back to the desired state.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing from state stops management, unreviewed code changes hide drift, and ignoring it leaves differences.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: A resource attribute is changed by an external system and Terraform should not revert it. What should be configured?
questions.correct_rationale: ignore_changes tells Terraform not to manage that attribute's updates.
questions.distractor_summary: prevent_destroy, create_before_destroy, and depends_on serve other purposes.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: Which command lists the resources tracked in state?
questions.correct_rationale: state list shows resource addresses in state.
questions.distractor_summary: output shows outputs, and fmt and validate do not read state.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: A resource must be renamed in code without recreating it. What is the recommended method?
options: Add a moved block from the old address to the new address
questions.correct_rationale: Moved blocks record refactors in code and update state.
questions.distractor_summary: Destroy and recreate causes downtime, manual edits are risky, and aliases are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: What does terraform state rm do?
options: Destroys the resource in the cloud
Removes a resource from state so Terraform stops managing it, without destroying the real object
questions.correct_rationale: state rm forgets a resource but leaves it running.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not destroy, delete code, or format.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: A resource should stop being managed by Terraform but stay in the cloud, and the change should be reviewed in code. What should be used?
options: A removed block with lifecycle { destroy = false }
questions.correct_rationale: Removed blocks forget resources declaratively without destroying them.
questions.distractor_summary: destroy deletes the resource, removing providers breaks runs, and fmt does nothing.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: Which command shows detailed attributes of one resource in state?
questions.correct_rationale: state show prints a resource's attributes.
questions.distractor_summary: state list shows names, and output or validate do not show resource details.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: Two resources must be swapped between modules during refactoring. Which approach is safest?
options: Deleting state and importing everything again
Manual edits of the state JSON
moved blocks for each address change, reviewed in a plan
questions.correct_rationale: moved blocks make refactoring visible and safe.
questions.distractor_summary: Re-importing is slow, manual edits risk corruption, and disabling locks is unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 6c Configure remote state using the backend block
questions.question: Which backend stores state in a Google Cloud Storage bucket?
questions.correct_rationale: The gcs backend stores state in Cloud Storage and supports locking.
questions.distractor_summary: azurerm, s3, and local target other storage.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: The team wants to see drift without changing infrastructure and record the current real values in state. What should they run?
questions.correct_rationale: Refresh-only applies update state to match reality without changing resources.
questions.distractor_summary: A normal apply changes infrastructure, destroy deletes, and fmt formats.

questions.subdomain: 6d Manage resource drift and Terraform state
questions.question: Which command replaced the deprecated terraform refresh as the recommended way to update state?
questions.correct_rationale: Refresh-only mode lets you review changes before updating state.
questions.distractor_summary: The other commands serve different purposes.

questions.subdomain: 6b Describe state locking
questions.question: A long apply is running when another engineer starts a plan against the same state. What should happen with a locking backend?
options: The second operation waits or fails because the state is locked
Both write to state at once
The second operation deletes the lock
questions.correct_rationale: Locks keep one write operation at a time.
questions.distractor_summary: Concurrent writes are prevented, and locks are not deleted or runs cancelled automatically.

questions.subdomain: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace
questions.question: What does importing a resource do?
options: Brings an existing real-world object under Terraform management by adding it to state
Creates a new copy of the resource
questions.correct_rationale: Import links existing infrastructure to Terraform addresses.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not copy, delete, or download modules.

questions.subdomain: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace
questions.question: A team wants to import resources in a way that can be reviewed in a plan. What should they use?
options: An import block in configuration with to and id arguments, then terraform plan and apply
questions.correct_rationale: Import blocks make imports part of the normal plan and apply workflow.
questions.distractor_summary: state rm forgets resources, destroy deletes them, and fmt formats.

questions.subdomain: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace
questions.question: Many existing resources need configuration written for import. What can help generate it?
questions.correct_rationale: Terraform can generate configuration for imported resources as a starting point.
questions.distractor_summary: output, graph, and console do not generate resource configuration.

questions.subdomain: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace
questions.question: What is required before running the terraform import CLI command for a resource?
options: A resource block in configuration with the matching address
questions.correct_rationale: The CLI import command needs a destination address in configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting state, new providers, and tags are not required.

questions.subdomain: 7a Import existing infrastructure into your Terraform workspace
questions.question: After importing, the plan shows changes to the imported resource. What does this mean?
options: The configuration does not exactly match the real resource, so it should be adjusted before applying
The resource will be deleted for sure
questions.correct_rationale: Planned changes show differences between code and reality.
questions.distractor_summary: Import succeeded, deletion is not implied, and state is not necessarily corrupted.

questions.subdomain: 7b Use the CLI to inspect state
questions.question: Which command prints outputs in JSON for scripts?
questions.correct_rationale: output -json provides machine-readable outputs.
questions.distractor_summary: The other commands do not output values in JSON.

questions.subdomain: 7b Use the CLI to inspect state
questions.question: Engineers need a human-readable view of all resources and attributes in state. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: show displays the full state in readable form.
questions.distractor_summary: validate, fmt, and init do not display state.

questions.subdomain: 7b Use the CLI to inspect state
questions.question: Which command lists the providers required by the configuration and modules?
questions.correct_rationale: terraform providers shows provider requirements and the module tree.
questions.distractor_summary: version shows the CLI version, and output or state rm are unrelated.

questions.subdomain: 7c Use verbose logging
questions.question: Which environment variable enables detailed Terraform logs?
questions.correct_rationale: TF_LOG sets the log level, such as TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, or ERROR.
questions.distractor_summary: The other names are not used for logging.

questions.subdomain: 7c Use verbose logging
questions.question: Logs must be written to a file for a support ticket. What should be set?
options: TF_LOG to a level and TF_LOG_PATH to a file path
questions.correct_rationale: TF_LOG_PATH writes logs to a file when logging is enabled.
questions.distractor_summary: TF_VAR sets variables, TF_DATA_DIR changes the data folder, and TF_INPUT controls prompts.

questions.subdomain: 7c Use verbose logging
questions.question: Only provider-related logs are needed, not the core logs. What can be set?
options: TF_LOG_PROVIDER, while TF_LOG_CORE controls core logs separately
questions.correct_rationale: Separate variables control core and provider logging.
questions.distractor_summary: OFF disables logs, PATH sets the file, and CLI_ARGS adds arguments.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: What is HCP Terraform?
options: A HashiCorp-managed service that runs Terraform, stores state, and adds collaboration and governance features
questions.correct_rationale: HCP Terraform manages runs, state, and team workflows.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a VM provider, editor, or language version.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: A configuration should run its plans and applies in HCP Terraform from the CLI. What is needed?
options: A cloud block naming the organization and workspace, and terraform login for credentials
questions.correct_rationale: The cloud block and login connect the CLI to HCP Terraform.
questions.distractor_summary: Local backends, aliases, and moved blocks do not connect to HCP Terraform.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: Which run workflows does HCP Terraform support?
options: Only manual uploads of state files
questions.correct_rationale: HCP Terraform offers three main run workflows.
questions.distractor_summary: Email, uploads, and on-premises only are not its workflows.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: Runs in HCP Terraform must reach private resources in a data center. What can be used?
options: Public IPs on all private systems
HCP Terraform agents running inside the private network
Copying state to the data center
questions.correct_rationale: Agents execute runs from within private networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs add risk, disabling runs loses features, and copying state does not help.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: What does a VCS-driven workspace do when a pull request is opened?
options: It runs a speculative plan and reports the result to the pull request
It applies changes immediately to production
questions.correct_rationale: Speculative plans give feedback before merge.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not apply immediately, delete the workspace, or ignore PRs.

questions.subdomain: 8a Use HCP Terraform to create infrastructure
questions.question: Cloud credentials for HCP Terraform runs should be short-lived. What feature supports this?
options: Dynamic provider credentials using workload identity tokens
Static keys stored as plain variables
questions.correct_rationale: Dynamic credentials avoid long-lived secrets.
questions.distractor_summary: Static or embedded keys and shared passwords are risky.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: What are policy as code features in HCP Terraform used for?
options: Enforcing rules on plans, using Sentinel or OPA policies, before apply
questions.correct_rationale: Policies check plans against organizational rules.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not format, store modules, or create providers.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: A company wants to block plans that create untagged resources. What should be used?
options: A Sentinel or OPA policy set applied to the relevant workspaces
questions.correct_rationale: Policies can deny runs that break rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Comments, defaults, and fmt do not enforce rules.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: What is the HCP Terraform private registry used for?
options: Sharing approved modules and providers privately within an organization
questions.correct_rationale: The private registry distributes internal modules and providers.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not for state, websites, or secrets.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: Policy results should warn on some rules and block on others. What policy enforcement levels support this?
options: Only one level that always blocks
Levels based on the time of day
questions.correct_rationale: Enforcement levels allow warnings or blocking.
questions.distractor_summary: There are several levels, and file size or time are not levels.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: What are run tasks in HCP Terraform?
options: Integrations that call external services, such as security scanners, during a run
questions.correct_rationale: Run tasks extend runs with external checks.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not calendar items, pods, or defaults.

questions.subdomain: 8b Describe HCP Terraform collaboration and governance features
questions.question: Different teams need different access to workspaces. How is this managed?
options: Using state file permissions on laptops
Teams with workspace or project permissions, such as read, plan, write, or admin
questions.correct_rationale: Team-based permissions control access.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared accounts, broad owner access, and laptop permissions are unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 8c Organize and use HCP Terraform workspaces and projects
questions.question: What does an HCP Terraform workspace contain?
options: Its own state, variables, run history, and settings for one configuration instance
questions.correct_rationale: Workspaces separate infrastructure instances.
questions.distractor_summary: They hold more than repos, binaries, or docs.

questions.subdomain: 8c Organize and use HCP Terraform workspaces and projects
questions.question: Many workspaces need the same cloud credentials and settings. What should be used?
options: Copy variables into each workspace by hand
A variable set applied to those workspaces or a project
